prerequisites: Basic knowledge of using PCs, especially installing programs under the Windows operating system (alternative operating systems are also possible)
Differential and integral calculus of several variables
Positive completion of StEOP (Study Introductory and Orientation Phase) for the courses 3,0/2,0 VU Numerical Methods in Engineering 1 and 3,0/2,0 VU Numerical Methods in Engineering 2

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to understand and apply fundamental programming concepts in Python and independently solve basic numerical problems in mechanical engineering.
They learn to design, implement, and test simple programs, and to use relevant Python libraries applied in engineering.
Students have basic knowledge of numerical methods for engineering applications.
They understand the principles of numerical arithmetic and numerical linear algebra, as well as central procedures for solving nonlinear equation systems.

They are able to appropriately apply numerical methods for interpolation, approximation, differentiation, integration, and for solving initial and boundary value problems, and critically evaluate their results.
Plan, design, implement, and test simple programs.
Systematically analyze and precisely formulate requirements for algorithmic solutions.
Purposefully plan and execute effective solution approaches for given tasks.
Structurally present the fundamentals of numerical arithmetic and numerical linear algebra.
Conceptually explain methods for solving nonlinear equation systems and apply them reliably in calculations.
Appropriately handle discrete data using interpolation and approximation.
Select and correctly apply numerical methods for differentiation and integration.
Analyze numerical methods for solving initial and boundary value problems and assess their accuracy and stability.
Plan and algorithmically implement software projects in the engineering field.
Present work results appropriately for the audience.
Systematically examine one's own learning progress and open clarification needs.
Present numerical solution approaches and results clearly, structured, and comprehensibly.
Critically reflect on computational procedures and results and professionally classify their limitations.
Independently work on mathematical-numerical problems and systematically structure solution paths.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and basics of procedural and object-oriented programming
Inputs and outputs, exception handling, testing
Graphical user interfaces and network communication
Methods for solving nonlinear equation systems
Solution of boundary and eigenvalue problems
Boundary value problems (in particular discretization using the finite difference method)
Initial value problems (in particular time-stepping methods)
teaching_methods: Lectures supported by electronic media and examples
Self-study through writing homework assignments in the form of programs
Exercises supported by staff and tutors
Introduction to the software development environment
Discussion of problems during exercises and consultation hours with tutors
Interaction with instructors and other participants via the e-learning platform
assessment_rules: For 'Digital Tools', assessment is based on continuous monitoring of learning progress and colloquia. For 'Numerical Methods', the examination modalities are to be specified in the information system for studies and teaching for each course before the start of the semester.
